nodes.label: FitResult NamedTuple pattern
nodes.rationale: Bundles samples with their own column labels via a .column(name) method so a caller can't pair a samples array with the wrong labels constant -- replaced module-level PLAIN_LABELS/PARALLAX_LABELS/LABELS constants after that exact mismatch caused a live IndexError in mcmc_fit_binary.py.

nodes.label: get_t0_par() cache-bootstrap pattern
nodes.rationale: Replaced an inline try/except cache block that silently computed t0_par two different ways (posterior median on cache hit, curve_fit point estimate on cache miss) depending on whether a file happened to exist -- a self-contained function now always returns the posterior median regardless of machine state.

nodes.label: Shared plotting/MCMC helpers ("do not re-copy")
nodes.rationale: Prefer one shared implementation over copy-pasted plotting/MCMC logic across scripts -- but explicitly warns against forcing an abstraction over a real difference: plot_fit_panels() was deliberately NOT built on the standardized-residual helpers because that would have hidden OGLE's real ~4x-better photometric precision behind MOA's when both instruments shared one panel (caught by the user, not by inspection).

nodes.label: Output layout convention
nodes.rationale: raw_lc/, fit_lc/, hist_plots/, corner_plots/ hold only the regular pipeline's canonical outputs; everything from scratch/ scripts writes there instead, enforcing the same code/output separation as the scratch/ convention.

nodes.label: scratch/ one-time-script convention
nodes.rationale: Keeps one-time/dev-script code and its output separated from the regular pipeline so scratch experiments (2L1S search, MulensModel cross-checks) don't pollute the canonical output directories; a script's code and output path move out together only when it graduates into the pipeline.

nodes.label: "User writes, Claude reviews" collaboration mode
nodes.rationale: The default mode per CLAUDE.md's guiding-role rule; explicitly overridden session-by-session for scoped pieces (quintic/root-finding core in session 3, full parallax propagation to O-03-BLG235 in session 9) at the user's direct request.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ relocation into microlensing/
nodes.rationale: The knowledge graph had been living one directory level outside the project (Desktop-level graphify-out/), which CLAUDE.md's outside-folder-access rule flagged as needing explicit user sign-off; rebuilt from scratch scoped to just microlensing/ per explicit request, old Desktop-level copy left in place at the time (later found already gone).

nodes.label: networkx (erroneously listed, unused, dropped)
nodes.rationale: Not imported by any script in the repo; likely an artifact of graphify's own setup in this venv rather than a pipeline dependency -- dropped from requirements.txt in session 9's cleanup.

nodes.label: "Bad chi2 can come from upstream issues, not the model" pattern
nodes.norm_label: "bad chi2 can come from upstream issues, not the model" pattern
nodes.rationale: Session 5 explicitly names this as a shared lesson between two distinct findings that session: the O-03-BLG235 frozen-calibration bug and MOA-2019-BLG-008's mag_err underestimation -- a catastrophically bad chi2 can come entirely from something upstream of the physical model (flux calibration; error-bar normalization) rather than indict the model or the search algorithm.

nodes.label: O-03-BLG235 calibrate-once-then-fit pipeline
nodes.rationale: OGLE (calibrated magnitude) and MOA (template-relative differential flux) can't be compared directly, so a joint PSPL fit is run once to invert both onto a shared magnification A(t) scale; this freezes the flux calibration at a point estimate, tightening downstream posteriors by not propagating calibration uncertainty -- and was later shown to bias 2L1S searches (chi2 31,982 vs 1,953 at Bond et al.'s parameters).

nodes.label: Rule: Claude acts in guiding role, user writes code
nodes.norm_label: rule: claude acts in guiding role, user writes code

nodes.label: MOA-2019-BLG-008 mag_err underestimation
nodes.rationale: Raw KMT mag_err column (median 0.006 mag) understates real point-to-point scatter (~0.1-0.2 mag) by 16-49x, a known property of raw KMTNet/pySIS photometry -- confirmed model-independently via a flat-line baseline fit (chi2/dof=2441) before ever indicting the lensing model itself; needs error-bar rescaling before fits mean anything, still unaddressed.

nodes.norm_label: rule: ask permission for files outside microlensing/

nodes.label: Rule: confirm ponytail active before writing/editing code
nodes.norm_label: rule: confirm ponytail active before writing/editing code

nodes.label: Annual parallax (Gould 2004 geocentric formalism)
nodes.rationale: Plain PSPL didn't fit real data well (O-05-BLG086: chi2/dof=2.14, residuals clustered in time windows) -- motivated adding piE_N/piE_E via Earth's orbital motion rather than accepting the unmodeled-physics residual pattern.

nodes.label: "Zero out new params to recover old special case" reuse trick
nodes.norm_label: "zero out new params to recover old special case" reuse trick
nodes.rationale: First used for lc_models.plain_flux()/plain_magnitude() (piE_N=piE_E=0 collapses the parallax terms exactly), then explicitly generalized one level up in session 9 to an entire calibration fit: fit_joint_pspl() with delta_sN/delta_sE fixed at zero recovers the pre-parallax model as an exact special case, avoiding a second near-duplicate chi2 function.

nodes.label: Central open question restated (session 1): tE can't separate mass from distance
nodes.norm_label: central open question restated (session 1): te can't separate mass from distance
nodes.rationale: Session 1's stated central open question: PSPL's fitted parameters (t0,u0,tE,fs,fb) alone cannot give a lens mass or distance -- tE conflates angular Einstein radius and relative proper motion with no way to separate them from single-band photometry alone. Directly motivated session 2's estimate_mass() work.

nodes.label: Prior-based lens mass estimate (M_lens)
nodes.rationale: Pairs each posterior tE sample with Monte Carlo draws from assumed mu_rel (log-normal) and D_L (naive uniform line-of-sight, not a real Galactic density model) priors, since tE alone can't fix mass. Explicitly flagged as the single biggest caveat in the pipeline and only illustrative, not a real mass measurement.

nodes.label: Mass-distance-velocity degeneracy (central open question)
nodes.rationale: tE alone conflates the angular Einstein radius and relative proper motion, so it can't fix a lens mass or distance without finite-source effects, parallax, or independent proper motion -- this is exactly why brown-dwarf-mass lenses are hard to identify from microlensing alone; the whole project exists to make this degeneracy visible, not hide it behind a point estimate.

nodes.label: Student-t robust likelihood
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Huber/sigma-clipping because the residual diagnostic showed a globally heavier-than-Gaussian error distribution (moderate excess kurtosis, MLE dof~6), not a small discrete outlier population -- a smooth down-weight fits the failure mode better than a hard cut.

nodes.label: BIC-based 2L1S-vs-PSPL model-comparison verdict plan
nodes.rationale: deltaBIC > 10 (Kass & Raftery) read as decisive; if only marginally under that threshold, the documented trigger is to escalate to a real Bayes factor via nested sampling (e.g. dynesty) rather than accept an ambiguous call. Still blocked as of session 9 on resolving the 2L1S search problem.

nodes.label: MulensModel (scratch-only oracle dependency)
nodes.rationale: Used only as a trusted independent oracle to cross-check binary_magnification and the parallax trajectory, never as a pipeline dependency -- this project's raw data itself comes from MulensModel's redistribution of OGLE/MOA photometry, but 2L1S/parallax are hand-rolled deliberately for the learning value.

nodes.label: sympy (scratch-only dev dependency)
nodes.rationale: Used once to symbolically derive the 2L1S quintic polynomial coefficients (removing transcription-error risk vs. hand-copying from Witt & Mao 1995), then the generated coefficients are hardcoded as plain numpy -- deliberately kept out of requirements.txt as a one-time dev tool, not a pipeline dependency.

nodes.label: mpmath (transitive sympy dependency, dropped)
nodes.rationale: Only present as sympy's own dependency; dropped from requirements.txt alongside sympy since neither belongs in the main pipeline's dependency list.

nodes.label: MulensModel cross-check convention-bug pattern (alpha 180deg offset)
nodes.rationale: A cross-check against a second independent implementation isn't automatically trustworthy just because it's 'the oracle' -- the first MulensModel comparison pass showed up to ~250x disagreement near caustics that looked like a real binary_magnification bug, but was actually a coordinate-convention bug in the comparison script itself (MulensModel's own alpha is shifted 180deg from its otherwise-documented convention). Explicitly described in CHANGELOG as the same category of failure as the u0-sign bug.

nodes.label: u0-sign / mirror-image degeneracy bug pattern
nodes.rationale: Because PSPL's u0 only enters the model squared, a bad/shared initial guess can make curve_fit converge to the wrong-sign mirror-image solution with an artificially tight posterior that still looks converged -- first hit while consolidating two MCMC scripts and silently reusing one dataset's hardcoded guess for another; only caught by comparing against a previous run's known values.

nodes.label: "Wrong-but-plausible result" recurring failure pattern
nodes.rationale: Repeatedly observed across sessions: neither chi2/dof nor posterior shape reveals a wrong model or wrong-sign fit on its own (OGLE-only single-lens fit to a binary event, u0-sign bug, near-miss cusp trajectories) -- wrongness only surfaces via an independent check (external data comparison, image-count geometry test, or a second implementation).

nodes.label: Per-dataset DATASETS dict guard
nodes.rationale: u0_guess/tE_guess are required, dataset-specific arguments (no shared default) kept in a DATASETS dict keyed by short name, specifically so a second dataset entry can't silently reproduce session 1's u0-sign bug.

nodes.label: Near-miss cusp solution search problem
nodes.rationale: After the calibration bug was fixed, multi-start and most MCMC runs converge to non-physical trajectories that never cross the caustic (no 3->5 image-count transition) yet score numerically better than Bond et al.'s published chi2 -- only catchable via the image-count check, not chi2 alone; still open as of session 9.
